name: Virtual Desktop
description: Gives agents their own Linux desktop (a Docker container) that they use by screenshot, mouse and keyboard.

command.name: vm
command.summary: Use your own Linux desktop by screenshot, mouse and keyboard.
command.usage: vm view | vm point <x> <y> — move the mouse to pixel coordinates in the screenshot (x across, y down, from the top-left corner) | vm point1k <x> <y> — move the mouse using a 0–1000 scale (0,0 is the top-left corner, 1000,1000 the bottom-right) | vm click [left|right|middle|double] — click where the mouse is | vm click <x> <y> [left|right|middle|double] | vm drag <x> <y> | vm type [--enter] <text> | vm type [--enter] (text in body) | vm key <combo> | vm scroll up|down|left|right [n] | vm wait [seconds] | vm launch <command> | vm run <command> | vm run (command in body) | vm upload <file or folder> [<desktop folder>] | vm download <desktop path> [<folder>] | vm status | vm stop | vm restart | vm reset
command.help:
Use your own Linux desktop (XFCE) by looking at screenshots and moving the
mouse and keyboard. It is your own computer: it keeps your files and the
programs you install, and you have passwordless sudo on it (run sudo apt-get update
before installing system packages).

Every result that shows a screenshot states:
  screen: 1280x800                 the desktop's size
  image 1280x800                   the screenshot's size (with its scale when
                                   it was shrunk to fit)
  window: <title>                  the focused window (omitted when none)
  pointer: (412, 488) px = (322, 610)‰ — over "Mozilla Firefox"
                                   where the mouse is on the screenshot, and
                                   the window under it
Coordinates are pixels of the LATEST screenshot.

Subcommands:
  vm view                     take a screenshot (starts the desktop if it is off)
  vm point <x> <y>            move the mouse to pixel coordinates in the screenshot (x across, y down, from the top-left corner)
  vm point1k <x> <y>          move the mouse using a 0–1000 scale (0,0 is the top-left corner, 1000,1000 the bottom-right), whatever the screenshot size
  vm click [button]           click where the mouse is; button is left (default), right, middle or double
  vm click <x> <y> [button]   move the mouse there, then click
  vm drag <x> <y>             press the left button where the mouse is, move to x y, release
  vm type [--enter] <text>    type the text into whatever is focused (--enter presses Return after)
  vm type [--enter]           type the body text
  vm key <combo>              press a key or combo: Return, Tab, Escape, ctrl+l, ctrl+shift+t, alt+F4, super
  vm scroll up|down|left|right [n]   turn the mouse wheel n clicks where the mouse is (default 5)
  vm wait [seconds]           wait for the screen to change and hold still (default 30s), then take a screenshot
  vm launch <command>         start a program on the desktop, e.g. vm launch firefox-esr https://example.com,
                              then take a screenshot
  vm run <command>            run a shell command (bash, as you, in your home folder) and return its exit
                              code and output; no screenshot. Quote the whole command when it has
                              spaces or shell operators, or put it in the body. It has a time limit.
                              End a command with & to leave something running (e.g. a dev server);
                              redirect its output to a file to read it later:
                              vm run "npm run dev > ~/dev.log 2>&1 &". Use vm launch for windowed programs
  vm upload <file or folder> [<desktop folder>]
                              copy from /me or /projects to the desktop (default ~/Desktop); a file
                              with the same name there is replaced
  vm download <desktop path> [<folder>]
                              copy a desktop file or folder to /me or /projects (default /me/downloads);
                              an existing name gets a number added
  vm status                   whether the desktop is running, its screen, memory and CPU limits; no screenshot
  vm stop                     power the desktop down; files and programs are kept, the next vm command
                              (except status and stop) starts it again
  vm restart                  reboot the desktop; files and programs are kept
  vm reset                    wipe the desktop back to a fresh install; everything on it is lost

Every action returns a fresh screenshot unless noted. Only the latest
screenshot stays visible; run vm view if unsure.

Already installed: Python 3 (python, pip, venv, pipx; pip install needs no
sudo), Node.js 24 with npm (npm install -g needs no sudo), git, gcc/make,
curl, jq, ripgrep (rg), fd, sqlite3, Firefox (firefox-esr), a terminal
(xfce4-terminal) and a text editor (mousepad).

Examples:
  vm view
  vm launch firefox-esr https://example.com
  vm point 412 488
  vm click
  vm click 640 360 double
  vm type --enter hello world
  vm key ctrl+l
  vm scroll down 3
  vm run "sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y cowsay"
  vm run "pip install requests && python -c 'import requests'"
  vm upload /me/report.md
  vm download ~/Downloads/data.csv
  vm stop

agent_config.label: Virtual desktop
agent_config.help:
Gives an agent its own Linux desktop that it uses with the mouse and keyboard.

Memory and CPUs are upper limits, not reserved: an idle desktop uses very little. Changing the screen, memory or CPUs restarts the desktop if it's running; its files and programs are kept.

If the desktop sits unused for the reminder time, the agent is asked whether to power it down.
